deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German lecture or study notes on ancient history, written in Kurrent script, and it continues the account of Macedonia begun on the previous page. The hand looks like a fair copy of lecture notes and may not be Gauss's own. There are therefore no derivations to reconstruct. Content, in order:

(1) The Argive (Temenid) colonists settled in Emathia. They held their ground against the natives, and their kings gradually ('nachgerade') enlarged their territory by subduing and expelling neighbours.

(2) Of the earliest kings only the names are known: Perdiccas, Argaeus, Philipp, Aeropus and Alcetas. The last of these is said to have died in 547 (BC).

(3) The kings then became entangled in wider world events. The Persians began their campaigns, and Macedonia was one of the first lands hit by their attacks.

(4) The kings of the time were too weak to resist, so they submitted to Darius Hystaspis (Darius I). During this period Amyntas (I) reigned, followed by his son Alexander I.

(5) The marginal note '†454' beside the last lines gives the death year of Alexander I (454 BC). This fits the next page, which dates Perdiccas II's reign to 454–413 and continues with Macedonian independence after 479.

The dates agree with the conventional chronology of the Argead kings used in early-19th-century handbooks: Alcetas d. 547, Alexander I d. c. 454. The bundle label 'HB.Lagrange1816' does not match the content; the folio appears to be bound-in historical notes.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page is non-mathematical.

Historically the dates follow the traditional (Eusebian-derived) chronology. Modern scholarship regards the early regnal dates (e.g. Alcetas d. 547) as legendary or uncertain, but that is a matter of the source, not a slip by the writer.
